limitations: Creators and developers are scripted reference agents (feasibility, labelled kind=scripted); participants are workstream-G rule-based need-driven adopters (crucible.innovation.adopt), not the workstream-B population.
The social channel used is the 4.0 forum; workstream-C platforms are not used yet.

Needs observables cover services, compute instances, declared capabilities and packages; content, communities, education, organisations and supply chains are not observed yet. complements comes from JSON-schema structure or world-configured relations.
Objective usefulness only for formats with a verifier (4.0 NEEDS and innovation.formats); subjective usefulness from diverse participant responses is not implemented here.
Adoption tracing counts Python-level calls into deps/<repo>/ (sys.setprofile); import-only use is not adoption.
The v5 registry is opt-in per world (caps config registry: true) so that 4.0 worlds keep their exact digests.
No substrate (workstream A) interface is used: it was not merged; packages are code repositories, not content-addressed artifacts, and cross-module effects use 4.0 hooks rather than bus.subscribe.
integration_notes: innovation/caps.py registers a subclass of the 4.0 Capabilities module under the same name 'caps' (MODULES['caps'] is replaced when crucible.innovation.modules is imported). All 4.0 endpoints/appliers/processes are inherited unchanged. With config registry: true, caps.search accepts {query} (v5) as well as {q} (4.0 behaviour) and the v5 endpoints exist; without it the v5 endpoints are withdrawn at install and caps.search keeps its exact 4.0 schema, so 4.0/3.0 tool catalogues, digests and logs are unchanged (tests/test_diagnostics.py 3.0 catalogue check passes).

To enable the v5 registry in a world: {'name': 'caps', 'config': {'registry': true}}; add 'needs' and 'pkg' (pkg depends on identity, bank, code, issues); 'adopt' and 'infra' are optional (participants, providers). innovation.worlds.innovation_spec builds such a world.

Population (B) integration point: world.hooks['needs_demand'](world) -> [(principal, capability, schema)] declares what individuals' tasks require; population individuals that call caps.search/caps.try/caps.adopt_service as their principals are measured by innovation.measure without changes.

Civilization (J) integration point: needs module config 'interfaces' (standard capability schemas) and 'edges' (relations as data) let a generator add couplings without code; chains/counterfactual helpers are innovation.measure.Stage/chain_record/counterfactual and innovation.scenarios.arms.

Primitives (A, section 1.5): pkg adds package/release/dependency records over 4.0 code repositories (the software_repository owner) and does not declare a second repository table; caps declarations add typed descriptions of 4.0 cloud services (the service owner).
